paper_title: Feedback Friction LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback
caption: : MMLU Pro confidence vs. accuracy
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and various accuracy metrics, including Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy. The x-axis represents Initial Confidence, with a linear scale ranging from 0.81 to 0.99, marked at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis represents Accuracy, also on a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: Final Accuracy, shown in blue with a solid line and square markers, starts at approximately 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81 and remains relatively stable, ending at around 0.96 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99; Δ Accuracy, depicted in orange with a dashed line and diamond markers, begins at about 0.38 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, decreases to around 0.07 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with notable fluctuations; Initial Accuracy, represented by a green dash-dot line with square markers, starts at approximately 0.5 at an Initial Confidence of 0.81, generally increases to around 0.9 at an Initial Confidence of 0.99, with some variability.
